ORDER:- The following Announcement was made on 13.08.2021 in the Revised Budget Speech 2021 - 2022:-

“New Urban Development Authorities will be formed for Madurai, the Coimbatore – Tiruppur Area, and for the fast growing Hosur area”.

2. In the letter read above, the Director of Town and Country Planning has furnished a proposal for constitution of Urban Development Authority for Madurai citing the following:-

i. Madurai city is the third largest city in Tamil Nadu. It spreads over an extent of 147.97 sq.km. It has a long tradition of culture and education. It has facilities such as international airport, railways, network of national highways with large trade and commercial activities. It is blessed with water reservoirs and the celebrated Vaigai river passes through the city as source of water supply and stabilised underground water table. In the last three decades, the city has been witnessing enormous growth in population thereby stressing the existing infrastructure amenities.

ii. The city of Madurai has been witnessing enormous growth in population for the past three decades. This growth in population has caused an uneven development in the city and its contiguous areas and has resulted in straining the existing infrastructure such as roads, health and educational facilities, water supply and sanitation.

2

iii. The Master Plan for Madurai which is under preparation will spell out a strategy for future development. In essence it will be a perspective plan which has anticipated the requirements of the Madurai planning area in all sectors of development.

iv. The magnitude of the tasks required and the action contemplated in this area unlikely that the current administrative set up in the area can co-ordinate the work of implementing agencies to plan and share the future development of the Madurai Urban Area in an orderly manner. It has, therefore become imperative to set up a separate Development Authority to ensure an orderly development in this area.

4.3 POWERLOOM SECTOR

The powerloom sector is one of the most significant segments of the

textile value chain. Among the different States in the south, Tamil Nadu has got

the largest concentration of powerlooms and the growth of this sector has been

phenomenal in the past three decades. In Tamil Nadu, Powerlooms are mainly

concentrated in the districts of Erode, Coimbatore, Tirupur, Salem, Namakkal,

Karur, Tiruvallur, Madurai, Tenkasi, and Virudhunagar. The majority of

powerlooms in Tamil Nadu are plain looms and a smaller number of shuttleless

looms. This sector requires modernisation and technological upgradation to

cope up with the severe competition in the domestic and overseas market.

The State has a large powerloom capacity which is in need of

upgrading/replacement. These looms primarily produce fabrics required for

Government schemes such as Supply of School Uniforms for students and

Distribution of Sarees and Dhoties. However, the powerloom industry is facing

the following challenges:

• Low productivity due to restricted loom width and speed.

● Excessive noise pollution in workplaces, causing stress for

workers.

● Fabric defects due to inconsistent shuttle speed.

● Primitive loom design, limiting production to basic weaves and

patterns, making premium fabric production impossible.

● Poor working conditions and low wages, leading to frequent

labour disputes demanding higher pay.

To address these issues and to meet international quality standards,

there is a constant demand to shift from shuttlelooms to advanced shuttleless

STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR TAKING ACTION AGAINST THE DELINQUENTS UNDER POCSO ACT, 2012, IN SCHOOLS

(DCPO) on the same day itself.

Importance of the Area

This area is very important for both migratory and resident birds, serving as a key stopover along the Central Asian Flyway with essential feeding and resting grounds for species like Herons, Egrets, Sandpipers, Terns, Greater and Lesser flamingos, Kentish plovers, Hanuman plover and Waders. Nearly 128 species of birds (migratory and residents) are recorded here. During the last Wetland bird census (2023-2024), 10,761 wetland birds were recorded in this area. Nearly, 47 plant species have been recorded in this area. Mangroves like Avicennia and Rhizophora around the Dhanushkodi Lagoon are crucial for stabilizing the coastline, preventing erosion and buffering storm surges. These plants also provide essential habitats for marine species and birds. The lagoon's diverse flora, including herbs, shrubs and trees, supports a rich environment for insects, birds and small mammals, enhancing both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

Designating these areas as a Bird Sanctuary will ensure protection of the resident, migratory birds and their habitats.
